title: 2.8 Transport in Plants
description: Transport in plants — every fact from the textbook.

questions.question: What are the transporting vessels of higher plants collectively called?
options: Fibres
Vascular bundles
Escherichia coli
Capillaries
questions.correctAnswer: Vascular bundles

questions.question: What are the two types of transporting vessels in plants?
options: Xylem and phloem
Leaf and flower
Salivary amylase
Cortex and pith
questions.correctAnswer: Xylem and phloem

questions.question: What does xylem transport?
options: The number of heart beats per minute
Food from leaves to roots
Returning nutrients to the ecosystem
Water and minerals from root to leaf
questions.correctAnswer: Water and minerals from root to leaf

questions.question: What type of cells make up xylem?
options: Using a single adult sheep cell and a process of nuclear transfer
Elongated dead cells joined end to end to form continuous vessels
They do not respond normally to the cell cycle controlling system
Nose, larynx, pharynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli
questions.correctAnswer: Elongated dead cells joined end to end to form continuous vessels

questions.question: What does phloem transport?
options: The stage of preparation where a cell exhibits growth and DNA synthesis
Organic matter (food) manufactured in the leaf to the rest of the plant
Daughter cells receive chromosomes that are the same in number and kind
A dome-shaped sheet of muscle separating thoracic from abdominal cavity
questions.correctAnswer: Organic matter (food) manufactured in the leaf to the rest of the plant

questions.question: What type of cells make up phloem?
options: Dead cells arranged end to end
Living cells arranged end to end
Elongated dead cells
Single cells with no connections
questions.correctAnswer: Living cells arranged end to end

questions.question: What is the transport of food through phloem called?
options: Photosynthesis
Transpiration
Absorption
Translocation
questions.correctAnswer: Translocation

questions.question: What substances does phloem transport?
options: Only amino acids
Nitrogen and phosphorus
Water and minerals
Sucrose and amino acids
questions.correctAnswer: Sucrose and amino acids

questions.question: Can phloem transport food up and down the plant?
options: No, only downward
Only horizontally
Yes, both up and down
The genetic parentage
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, both up and down

questions.question: What are sites of food production (sources) and sites of use or storage (sinks) connected by?
options: A living organism's behavior
Translocation through phloem
Outside the nuclear membrane
Olfactory nerves are damaged
questions.correctAnswer: Translocation through phloem

questions.question: Why is the stem of sugar cane so sweet?
options: By identifying the types and numbers of microscopic organisms found in ecosystem samples
From the non-living environment to living organisms and back to the non-living environment
Sugars synthesized in the leaf are converted to starch and accumulated in storage organs
If dried, crushed, and diluted in water they would kill snails at very low concentrations
questions.correctAnswer: Sugars synthesized in the leaf are converted to starch and accumulated in storage organs

questions.question: What are examples of storage organs in plants?
options: Because materials are found in limited amounts
The use of biological knowledge to manage life
Root and stem tubers, leaves, seeds and fruits
Bananas, oranges, potatoes, chicken, and liver
questions.correctAnswer: Root and stem tubers, leaves, seeds and fruits

questions.question: How does water from the soil first enter the root?
options: It grows straight because rotation overcomes gravity
A unit character such as height, body colour, or sex
The most prestigious agricultural prize in the world
Through root hairs, which are elongated single cells
questions.correctAnswer: Through root hairs, which are elongated single cells

questions.question: What do root hairs provide that allows more water to enter the root?
options: A selective filter
Liquid droplets only
A waterproof layer
A large surface area
questions.correctAnswer: A large surface area

questions.question: What is the process of water and minerals entering the root called?
options: Photosynthesis
Translocation
Transpiration
Absorption
questions.correctAnswer: Absorption

questions.question: How does water pass from cell to cell across the root?
options: Either by osmosis across the cell membrane and cytoplasm or by diffusion along the porous cell wall
For dual purpose: harvest the legumes as a crop and use fixed nitrogen in soil for non-legume crops
A field of science used to gather and analyze evidence to establish facts used in a legal scenario
More auxin on the shaded part of the root inhibits cell elongation compared to the illuminated side
questions.correctAnswer: Either by osmosis across the cell membrane and cytoplasm or by diffusion along the porous cell wall

questions.question: Does water pass actively or passively across the root cells?
options: Passively (without spending additional energy)
After the four stages of mitosis are completed
Unsaturated ones are solid at room temperature
Stomach acid from entering the small intestine
questions.correctAnswer: Passively (without spending additional energy)

questions.question: What is the main force responsible for pulling water from root to leaves through xylem?
options: Osmotic pressure
Capillary action
Complement cascade
Transpiration pull
questions.correctAnswer: Transpiration pull

questions.question: What creates the transpiration pull?
options: Four identical daughter cells
Soil water pressure
The total number of organisms
Water evaporating from leaves
questions.correctAnswer: Water evaporating from leaves

questions.question: What helps resist the downward pull of gravity on water in the xylem?
options: Which antigens are on the surface of red blood cells
Their narrow needle-shaped leaves with thick cuticle
Adhesion of water to the cell wall by hydrogen bonds
A process by which a cell loses its genetic material
questions.correctAnswer: Adhesion of water to the cell wall by hydrogen bonds

questions.question: What helps hold together the column of water within xylem cells?
options: No, they do not shade their leaves in winter or summer
The vein (transporting vessels) and supportive tissues
Symbiotic nitrogen fixation and non-symbiotic fixation
Cohesion due to hydrogen bonds between water molecules
questions.correctAnswer: Cohesion due to hydrogen bonds between water molecules

questions.question: In what form do minerals enter the root?
options: Molecular form
Periodontal ligament
Ionic (charged) form
Gaseous form
questions.correctAnswer: Ionic (charged) form

questions.question: How are minerals taken up when concentration is higher in plant cells than outside?
options: The atmosphere (air), hydrosphere (water), and lithosphere (soil)
Food chain follows a single path, food web follows multiple paths
Actively by cell spending energy against a concentration gradient
Rainfall at a distance or melting ice or snow from high mountains
questions.correctAnswer: Actively by cell spending energy against a concentration gradient

questions.question: What is the ringing or girdling experiment used to demonstrate?
options: Water transport through xylem
Transpiration
Food transport through phloem
Root absorption
questions.correctAnswer: Food transport through phloem

questions.question: What happens in the ringing experiment?
options: Unilateral stimulus causing unequal production or distribution of growth hormone resulting in unequal growth
A type of nuclear division where duplicated chromosomes are distributed between two identical daughter cells
A ring of bark with the phloem is removed, leaving xylem as the only vessel connecting upper and lower parts
Hydrophilic heads lie in watery solutions outside the membrane, hydrophobic tails form an impermeable layer
questions.correctAnswer: A ring of bark with the phloem is removed, leaving xylem as the only vessel connecting upper and lower parts

questions.question: What is observed in the upper part of the girdled area after a few days?
options: Skeletal muscle action, respiratory movement, and smooth muscle contraction
Because glucose would dissolve and compromise the cell's osmotic properties
The amount of energy, biomass, or number of organisms at each trophic level
A swelling due to accumulation of food materials translocated from the leaf
questions.correctAnswer: A swelling due to accumulation of food materials translocated from the leaf

questions.question: What are aphids?
options: Active transport where living phloem cells use energy obtained by metabolic process
Water molecules are attracted to ions and polar molecules, causing them to separate
A symbiotic association that forms root nodules where $N_2$ is reduced into ammonia
Soft-bodied insects that use piercing and sucking mouth parts to feed on phloem sap
questions.correctAnswer: Soft-bodied insects that use piercing and sucking mouth parts to feed on phloem sap

questions.question: What will ultimately happen to a plant that is ringed?
options: In waterlogged soils (anoxic), layers of sediments in lakes and oceans
Chemotherapy, sometimes followed by radiation and stem-cell transplant
It will die because of disruption of food transport through the phloem
That all species had been created by God at the beginning of the world
questions.correctAnswer: It will die because of disruption of food transport through the phloem

questions.question: Which part of a ringed plant dies first?
options: The root
The shoot tip
The leaves
The stem
questions.correctAnswer: The root

questions.question: Why does the root of a ringed plant die first?
options: A strip of actively dividing young cells (cambium)
Glucose, amino acids, water, vitamins, and alcohol
Because supply of food to the root is discontinued
They prevent soil erosion by holding soil together
questions.correctAnswer: Because supply of food to the root is discontinued

questions.question: What type of transport occurs through the phloem?
options: Active transport where living phloem cells use energy obtained by metabolic process
Water molecules are attracted to ions and polar molecules, causing them to separate
It is a component of the peroxidase enzyme, a lysosomal enzyme for killing bacteria
Nitrogen fixation, ammonification, nitrification, assimilation, and denitrification
questions.correctAnswer: Active transport where living phloem cells use energy obtained by metabolic process
